newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-EDBERG COMFORTABLE WINNER AGAINST HENMAN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-EDBERG COMFORTABLE WINNER AGAINST HENMAN.

text.p: Stefan Edberg cruised to an easy 6-4 6-2 win over Tim Henman of Britain in the opening round of the $2.25 million Stuttgart Open on Monday.
The Swede, who plans to quit tennis at the end of the year, needed 90 minutes to eliminate Henman, a Czech Open semifinalist last week but still searching for his first ATP Tour win.
Edberg, who has been suffering from a cold in the last week, said he was pleased to have overcome the first hurdle here so easily.
"The first match of a tournament is always very tricky," he said. "I felt very comfortable tonight."

The Swede, ranked 17th in the world, prised open a close first set by breaking serve to go ahead 5-4 and then holding his own serve. That seemed to deflate Henman, who won just two of the next eight games.
"It wasn't really as exciting as I thought it was going to be," Edberg added.
Edberg will now face Goran Ivanisevic of Croatia in the second round on Wednesday.
